commit.message:
fix: enforce per-user Hyperliquid keys and surface provisioning failures

Execution already loaded the per-user API-wallet credential, but three gaps
let a mis-provisioned account appear healthy and then fail opaquely at order
time:

- provision_agent_credential never verified the write persisted; a silent
  Redis failure left the UI on "connected" with no key stored
- a missing or mismatched key raised 403, but execute_short_order's blanket
  except re-wrapped it as 503 "runtime not ready", hiding the cause
- a credential that resolved to the legacy shared env API wallet would have
  signed with the operator key

Now: provisioning reads the credential back and raises unless it persisted;
execution surfaces clear per-user errors (HYPERLIQUID_NO_USER_KEY /
HYPERLIQUID_KEY_MISMATCH / HYPERLIQUID_SHARED_KEY_REFUSED) and refuses to
sign with the shared operator key; /healthz reports whether the encryption
key and Redis storage are configured. Provision and execute log the wallet,
master, stored API wallet, and whether the credential was found/stored.

Tests: new test_user_key_isolation.py pins two masters signing each with
their own key, the missing-key 403, the shared-key refusal, and that a 403
is not masked as a 503; test_sizing.py updated for the 5 Settings fields
added in 0d9a4c3.

fix: sign Hyperliquid agent approval on the wallet's current chain

Approve protection failed with "chainId should be same as current
chainId" because the EIP-712 domain hardcoded Arbitrum (42161/421614)
while the wallet was connected to Flare or Coston2. Wallets refuse to
sign a typed-data domain that names a different chain than the one
they are on.

approveAgent is an off-chain Hyperliquid L1 action, so no transaction
is broadcast to the chain being signed on. Hyperliquid only requires
that the domain and the signatureChainId in the action agree, so both
now carry the wallet's current chain and the signature verifies.

Also:
- Report Hyperliquid's own rejection reason instead of a fixed message.
- Require authorizedAt before protection reads Ready.
- Block arming while approval is outstanding, with a reason in the UI,
  instead of failing later at execution.
- Split the execute route's 403 into not-enabled, awaiting-approval,
  and wrong-wallet cases.

fix: name the missing variable when Hyperliquid setup fails

Configuration failures in the provisioning route all surfaced as
"Hyperliquid protection could not be prepared", which hid whether the
signer URL was absent, non-HTTPS, or the signer itself rejected the
call. Configuration errors now name the offending variable while
genuine signer failures keep the generic message.

feat: consumer-friendly Hyperliquid protection flow

Replace the developer-config form on Auto-Hedge with a single
"Enable Hyperliquid protection" action.

Users no longer enter a master account, API wallet, personal signer
URL, or signer auth token. Enabling now runs one flow: the server
provisions a per-user Hyperliquid agent wallet through RippleFI's own
signer, the user signs a single approveAgent message from their own
wallet, and the app stores only the linkage and authorization status.

The signer URL and token become server-only app infrastructure. Each
user still trades from their own Hyperliquid account via their own
approved agent wallet, and the signer rejects any request whose agent
is not authorized for that account, so a shared operator account is
never used to trade on a user's behalf.

UI is reduced to one button plus Not connected / Needs approval /
Ready status chips.
